lede: Thai · อักษรไทย accounts for 72 catalogued manuscripts, 25 of them flagged research-priority. It clusters in Chiang Rai (12% of the corpus for this script), ahead of Lampang and Phrae. By support it leans to mulberry paper (saa) · กระดาษสา (29%) over khoi paper · กระดาษข่อย (15%). Dated witnesses run 1937–2007 CE (20 of 72 carry a date).

findings.title: The market's crown jewels
findings.gloss: The twelve most valuable objects catalogued from the living market, topped by one listed at 1,500,059 THB.

findings.title: The minority hands: scripts beyond Tham Lanna
findings.gloss: Almost the whole collection is written in Tham Lanna.

findings.title: Already legible to a machine
findings.gloss: The manuscripts with the most recognised Thai text — the leading edge of the whole point: making a living tradition readable to a model and not only to a scholar.

findings.title: Words the market speaks that the manuscripts never wrote
findings.gloss: These terms are common in the living market yet appear in no catalogued manuscript — proof that the tradition is not a closed archive but a language still adding words.
